items.followUp: Write the subshell electronic configuration of silicon (Si, atomic number 14).

rubric.why: The subshell configuration must place all 13 electrons correctly.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the complete configuration; no marks for an incomplete or incorrect configuration.

modelAnswer: Al has atomic number 13, so it has 13 electrons.

items.followUp: What are meant by a group and a period in the Periodic Table?

rubric.why: Groups are the vertical columns of the Periodic Table.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying groups as vertical columns.

rubric.why: Periods are the horizontal rows of the Periodic Table.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying periods as horizontal rows.

modelAnswer: Groups are the vertical columns in the Periodic Table.
Periods are the horizontal rows in the Periodic Table.

items.followUp: State any two features of the modern Periodic Table.

rubric.why: The long-form Periodic Table arranges elements according to increasing atomic number.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that elements are arranged by increasing atomic number.

rubric.why: The long-form table has seven periods and eighteen groups and is divided into blocks.
rubric.description: States another feature of the long-form table.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one correct feature, such as seven periods, eighteen groups, or division into blocks.

modelAnswer: Elements in the long-form Periodic Table are arranged in order of increasing atomic number.

items.followUp: Define a coordinate covalent bond and give an example involving the hydronium ion.

rubric.why: In a coordinate covalent bond, the shared pair is supplied by one atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that one atom donates both electrons of the shared pair.

rubric.why: Ammonium and hydronium ions are examples of coordinate covalent bonding.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example such as NH₄⁺ or H₃O⁺.

modelAnswer: A coordinate covalent bond is a covalent bond in which one atom donates both electrons of the shared pair.
Example: NH₃ + H⁺ → NH₄⁺; the nitrogen atom donates its lone pair.

items.followUp: Differentiate between polar and non-polar covalent bonds.

rubric.why: Polar covalent bonds involve unequal sharing of electrons, producing partial charges.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating unequal sharing of electrons or the resulting partial charges.

rubric.why: Non-polar covalent bonds involve equal sharing and do not have charged ends.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating equal sharing of electrons or absence of poles.

modelAnswer: In a polar covalent bond, electrons are shared unequally, producing partial charges on the atoms.
In a non-polar covalent bond, electrons are shared equally and no poles are formed.

items.followUp: What are intermolecular forces? Give one example.

rubric.why: Intermolecular forces act between separate molecules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that these forces act between molecules.

rubric.why: Hydrogen bonding, van der Waals forces, and dipole-dipole forces are examples.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any valid example of an intermolecular force.

modelAnswer: Intermolecular forces are forces of attraction between molecules.

items.followUp: Define diffusion and state the direction in which particles move during diffusion.

rubric.why: Diffusion involves the movement and mixing of particles.
rubric.description: Identifies diffusion as particle movement or mixing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing diffusion as the movement or mixing of particles.

rubric.why: Particles diffuse from a region of higher concentration to one of lower concentration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating movement from higher to lower concentration.

modelAnswer: Diffusion is the spontaneous movement and mixing of particles.
Particles move from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration.

items.followUp: What is the Kelvin scale, and how is it related to the Celsius scale?

rubric.why: The absolute temperature scale begins at absolute zero.
rubric.description: Identifies the zero point of the scale.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the scale begins at absolute zero (0 K or approximately −273°C).

rubric.why: Kelvin is the unit used on the absolute temperature scale.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the Kelvin scale or kelvin as its unit.

modelAnswer: The absolute temperature scale is the Kelvin scale, which begins at absolute zero (0 K, approximately −273°C).
